summary:
AmTree Lunar Navigator is an interactive tool that helps users explore possible landing sites near the Moon’s south pole. Using public NASA terrain data and calculations of the Sun’s and Earth’s positions, it shows when selected locations receive sunlight, face darkness, or have a clear view of Earth. Users can explore a 3D Moon, compare sites, and see how changing the arrival time affects conditions during a mission.

Built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, the project makes complex lunar data easier to understand. It is a prototype for exploring mission options and learning why both where and when we land matter.
details:
AmTree is an interactive web app for exploring where and when to land near the Moon’s south pole. Users can compare six lunar study points and representative locations within nine Artemis III candidate regions. The app offers a snapshot at a selected UTC time and a dynamic simulation over a custom date range. Users can switch between sunlight and Deep Space Network visibility when comparing locations, then open a location to inspect its terrain, charts, and animated maps.

The simulation combines NASA lunar elevation data from the Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) with NASA/JPL SPICE ephemerides. It compares the positions of the Sun and Earth with the local terrain horizon and estimates line of sight to Deep Space Network stations in Goldstone, Madrid, and Canberra. This matters because a site can have good sunlight for solar power but limited opportunities for direct communication with Earth. A shared timeline and an interactive 3D Moon let users see when both conditions are favorable and what changes if they choose a different site or date.

We built the interface with React, TypeScript, and Three.js. The Python simulation runs in the browser through Pyodide and CSPICE WebAssembly, without a separate calculation server. Users can export results as CSV for further analysis. AmTree is designed for early mission planning and education. It estimates sunlight and geometric visibility, not battery charge, radio link quality, or antenna availability.
